claims.text: The starting near-equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy is an as-cast, single-phase FCC material.
Annealing near-equiatomic FeCoNi at 700–800 °C for several hours and subsequently cooling or aging it will induce B2-type precipitation.
The induced B2 precipitates will be nanoscale and embedded within an FCC FeCoNi matrix.
Fine B2 precipitates provide magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning from the precipitates will increase the coercive field.
The annealed alloy will have greater coercivity than FeCoNi and the previously studied soft FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys.
B2 precipitation will have only a modest effect on saturation magnetization.
The heat treatment will preserve the alloy's near-equiatomic proportions and high configurational entropy.
A near-equiatomic FeCoNi composition has configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Retaining a high-entropy matrix will provide a favorable balance between magnetic strength and mechanical properties.
Annealing outside 700–800 °C may prevent the intended B2 precipitate formation.
Failure to preserve compositional balance may prevent the intended B2 precipitate formation.
If the intended B2 precipitates do not form, coercivity improvement may be minimal.
Composition fluctuations may affect the reproducibility of the phase structure and magnetic response.
FeCoNi, FeCoNiPd, and FeCoNiPt represent soft-ferromagnetic FeCoNi-based baselines.

contradictions.description: The proposed intervention calls for controlled cooling or aging after annealing to induce precipitates, whereas the discriminating experiment specifies quenching and does not include the stated aging step.
